findings.status: new conditional source-policy observation; supported reachability and unique identity pending central reconciliation
findings.first_contract: abutment_host says eligible contact lies at the exterior masonry face, never the wall centreline. For finite nonnegative wall thickness t, its actual test |signed_normal − t/2| ≤ t/2 + 0.18 admits signed_normal = 0 and all interior-side signed distances down to −0.18 m, if source, along-wall and vertical filters also pass. The nearest eligible host is then selected by arcade priority and distance.
findings.downstream: The inspected caller samples roof edge stations, calls abutment_host, then creates weathering and records host/support on accepted stations. It removes those samples, solids, interfaces and newly added bonds if an edge does not have every station hosted.
findings.condition: A supported roof edge or cut fragment must actually put a relevant station at such a centreline/interior point, pass all other filters and be selected over competing walls; the edge must survive later cleanup. None of those conditions, physical wrong contact, generation output, validator result or runtime effect has been demonstrated. The margin may be an intentional tolerance; resolve actual wall-contact policy before implementation.
findings.future_direction: Clarify whether signed exterior-side admission or a distinct tolerance should govern host selection; establish real accepted geometry and expected corner/cut policies before choosing a correction. Preserve deterministic host priority, legitimate tolerance and opening-cut rejection.

findings.status: current source refinement of prior open contact approximation policy; distinct effect and alias require central review
findings.first_contract: RoofContacts::touching decides an owner contact solely from greater-than-0.025-metre overlap of yaw-only axis-aligned bounds; those bounds ignore crossfall and longfall. The actual apron construction passes crossfall −0.10 radians and size Y=0.045, Z=0.34 into a checked CollisionCuboid, and ResolvedSolid retains those angles. Its full represented vertical extent is 0.045 cos(0.10) + 0.34 sin(0.10), whereas yaw_bounds uses 0.045. Axis-aligned bounds can also overlap without establishing an oriented-solid intersection.
findings.downstream: Returned owners become candidate JunctionBonds. Incomplete edge handling removes the bonds, and the separately inspected audit checks retained bonds through an alternative tower criterion or owner-pair geometry/area/gap metrics. Those later source checks have not been executed or shown to approve or repair a particular bond.
findings.condition: A supported station must produce a wall/roof owner set that differs materially from the intended exact physical contact and its edge must survive subsequent reconciliation; actual retained false or missing bond, later validator result, physical effect and output are unproved. This is a source and mathematical proxy observation, not a computed fixture or geometry run.
findings.future_direction: Determine intended contact authority and actual owner/edge acceptance; if physical contact is required, select a coherent fully oriented and appropriately tolerant narrow-phase policy rather than treating a broad envelope as proof. Preserve intended corner multi-owner junctions and checked errors.

findings.status: bounded current evidence for 059 q2257, not a new finding
findings.first_contract: The inspected primary roof loop assigns RoofAssemblyId(index+1), and attached-child creation passes that child assembly into append. Four fixed slots use low bits 0–3 and the face ID derives from 0xA tag | child.id<<16 | 0x4200 | slot. For child IDs below 2^45 this local child/slot expression is injective within that range; larger input bits can overlap fixed tag bits or be shifted out.
findings.condition: Actual supported roof-count bound, other ResolvedItemId namespaces, recipient uniqueness domains and downstream acceptance remain unproved. findings.status: connected historical producer propagation and parent-surface policy; no new count
findings.first_contract: After rectangle overlap and higher-base checks, the caller uses a clone of the first parent, derives four child corners and samples parent roof face heights for each endpoint. Missing sampled height falls back to parent recipe base; the record constructor retains the resulting raw polygon and support references. A later front-wall bond is emitted only when its looked-up parent owner exists.
findings.condition: Rectangle overlap is not a proof that every child corner is covered by a parent face, but no supported recipe is shown to produce a missing corner or an incorrect enclosure, and the intended meaning of the base fallback is unresolved. Four stored vertices do not by themselves prove a valid finite/nondegenerate polygon; no specific malformed supported input or later rendering failure shown.
findings.future_direction: Trace admitted roof recipes, parent support and enclosure geometry consumers; decide an explicit absent-parent-surface policy and preserve any intended outside-perimeter mode. Carry the accepted position owner across the retained record as needed without requiring extra wrappers in numerical kernels.

open_questions.question: Can a supported retained roof edge reach a selected host at its wall centreline or inside face within the signed-normal margin, and is this tolerance intended?
Can a supported rotated or crossfall roof weathering/host configuration make yaw-only AABB contact assign a materially wrong owner after complete-edge and audit checks?
What actual maximum roof assembly count, ID provenance and retained namespace prevent local tag overlap or cross-family enclosure ID collisions?
When an attached child rectangle overlaps but extends beyond parent faces, must each corner find a sampled parent height, or is parent-base fill an intended topology?
Can a front-wall source legitimately have a child whose parent owner lookup fails, and who owns missing bond or support disposition?

lenses.assessment: Parent roof samples and raw child corners enter retained enclosure polygons; native historical F001/RAW-SOURCE-002 already records this producer-to-retained-owner gap.
RoofAssemblyId, ResolvedItemId, GeometryOwnerId and SpatialBounds have distinct purposes; retain intentional native geometry calculations while tracing checked point ownership.
Actual child ID producer is sequential, local slots fixed; public wrappers and raw recipe values do not establish global roof-count, namespace, containment or finite-polygon policy.
Height sampling, packed shifts, signed wall offsets and yaw-only bounds each have distinct numerical contracts. Axis-aligned contact and centreline implications are conditional source observations.
Child parent link, four faces, support nodes, wall bond, contact samples and junction bonds form coupled state; fallback and incomplete-edge cleanup have separate policies.
Geometry owner, roof graph identity, wall source and native material roles are not interchangeable; common packed-id remedy does not establish alias.
The owner bounds map is derived from an input snapshot; no competing wall authority or mutation during its lifetime is shown. Owner pair checks remain separate from exact geometry.

Selected original and current bodies are byte-identical; whole historical snapshot and product behavior are not. Preserve host priority, weather edge rejection, deterministic IDs and inward graph support.
Tower versus wall abutment and WallSourceId variants select distinct host policies. No semantic boolean replacement established.
Assigned functions do not contain manual serialization or trait boilerplate whose replacement would safely simplify this contract.
Plan coordinates, scene heights, oriented solids, yaw bounds, owner IDs and physical contact represent different information; raw numeric kernel boundaries and retained state need distinct decisions.
Assigned source has no internal string-dispatch protocol. Existing human comments/diagnostics are not authority keys.
0.025 overlap, 0.18 wall clearance, area and angle tolerances carry different units and semantics. Evaluate actual calculation/error budgets, not blanket replacements.
